concepts_addressed: Owner Delivery Time as Scaling Constraint

frameworks.name: Owner-Operator vs. Subcontractor Trade-Offs Matrix
frameworks.definition: A decision framework weighing control/loyalty (owner-operator) against complexity/scaling challenges (subcontractor), anchored to the founder's personal goals and speed-to-scale requirements.

frameworks.name: 10-Stage Business Growth Roadmap (Zero to $100M+)
frameworks.definition: A stage-gate model identifying predictable constraint transitions as headcount increases, with 8 functional breakpoints and graduation criteria across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar.

claims.text: Owner-operator and subcontractor models present inverse trade-offs: owner-operator provides more control, loyalty, and stability but requires more oversight and personal responsibility; subcontractor model reduces control, increases flakiness and disloyalty, but transfers some execution burden.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Owner-operator concentrates accountability and visibility in founder; subcontractor model distributes execution but dilutes founder oversight.
bounded_by: Does not prescribe which model is universally better
Depends on founder's personal goals and business scaling speed target

claims.text: The choice between owner-operator and subcontractor models is determined by the founder's primary goal—whether optimizing for rapid growth, independent scalability, or quick exit—not by objective business metrics.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Goal clarity filters the relevant constraints; different goals eliminate different trade-offs from consideration.
bounded_by: Does not assume all founders have identical goals

claims.text: In rapidly scaling businesses (example: gym franchise vs. owner-operator scaling), the founder must ask both 'What is the business goal?' and 'How fast do we need to reach it?' because speed requirements reshape which trade-offs are acceptable.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.topic: Owner Delivery Time as Scaling Constraint
claims.mechanism: Time-to-scale urgency alters the cost-benefit calculus of ownership models; slow-growth strategies favor owner-operator (knowledge capture), fast-growth favors subcontractor/franchise (parallel execution).

claims.text: There exists a predictable 10-stage roadmap from zero to $100M+ revenue that fewer than 1% of companies complete, with each stage marked by constraint transitions across 8 business functions and graduation criteria that hold across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar contexts.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: As headcount increases, the binding constraint shifts predictably across functions (sales, operations, fulfillment, leadership); recognizing and graduating through these constraints enables continued growth.

examples.text: Zach Fine asked whether starting a lean remodeling company as owner-operator is better than hiring subcontractors. Hormozi response: both models have problems—subcontractor model creates loyalty and flakiness issues, owner-operator model creates oversight burden. The right answer depends on whether your goal is to build an enormous independent business or sell quickly.

A founder deciding between scaling their gym through owner-operator model versus franchising must first answer: What is my goal (build the best in niche, or exit quickly)? How fast must I reach it? These answers eliminate entire categories of trade-offs and make the model choice obvious.
examples.topic: Owner Delivery Time as Scaling Constraint

practices.text: Before selecting an ownership model (owner-operator vs. subcontractor/franchise), explicitly define your personal goal and your speed-to-scale target.
When scaling a remodeling or service business, understand the constraint symptoms and graduation criteria across the 10 stages of growth (available via acquisition.com/roadmap).
Evaluate each business model not as objectively better/worse, but as a choice between different categories of problems you will solve and problems you will accept.
